subject: NorthStarAI — bespoke availability variance & operational asks
messages:
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@northstarai.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: bespoke availability variance for NorthStarAI

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the demo last week. NorthStarAI runs low-latency inference for live personalization and we have a commercial need to get a tighter availability/response commitment than standard. We've put together a short requirements doc (attached). High-level ask: a bespoke availability variance that guarantees p95 inference latency <= 60ms for our production inference route (US + EU primary; global failover) with an operational runbook, on-call escalation path, and a clear credit formula if missed.

Key context:
- Peak: ~3.5k qps sustained during spikes, steady-state 800 qps
- Typical payload: short prompts (~60 tokens) + caching will help but prefix reuse is limited
- Security: SOC2 + data residency discussion in progress

Can Redwood support a limited pilot with a dedicated pool and an SLA addendum? If so we need an internal summary of constraints/cost uplift and an ops runbook to present to our procurement/legal.

Attachments: northstar_requirements_v2.pdf

Appreciate a quick alignment call — Jared
NorthStar AI — Head of Platform
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@northstarai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 14:30:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: bespoke availability variance for NorthStarAI

Jared — thanks for the clear ask and the doc. Looping in product/engineering/legal to scope feasibility. Quick clarifying Qs so we come prepared:
1) Is the 60ms p95 requirement a hard must-have for all regions or only the US primary?
2) Any hard SLA start date or preferred pilot window (next 30 days)?
3) Do you expect burst traffic from APAC or just baseline EU failover?

Proposed next steps:
- Internal triage (product, infra, legal) to produce a short feasibility note + cost delta
- 30-min alignment call this week with your engineering lead to review traffic profiles and RTOs

Marissa — can you own the commercial path (pilot terms + credits)? Grace/Vivek/Laura: can you weigh in with constraints and a preliminary ops ask by EOD Wed?

Thanks — Alex
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: bespoke availability variance for NorthStarAI

Alex / Jared,

Product take (short): we can support a p95 ~60ms on Dedicated reserved pools for short-input inference if we control model variant, quantization, and routing. Caveats:
- Cross-region failover (EU -> US) will add network hops; p95 could spike during failover windows. We can mitigate with active-active routing and warmed KV caches, but that requires a pre-provisioned footprint in EU and additional cache warming steps.
- For 3.5k qps spikes we need either larger reserved capacity or burst credits — both have cost implications.
- We should consider an operational runbook that includes: cache-warm threshold, degraded-model fallback (smaller model with similar quality), and a traffic-shedding policy for sustained overloads.

Requesting the customer's 7-day traffic histogram and the preferred failover tolerance (seconds to minutes). I've uploaded an internal feasibility checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleRunbook

If NorthStar will accept a staged SLA (pilot: 60ms p95 on US primary, EU evaluated in Phase 2), that materially reduces risk.

— Grace
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Mar 2028 16:20:34 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: bespoke availability variance for NorthStarAI

Alex / team,

Engineering reality check: achieving p95=60ms at 3.5k spike QPS is non-trivial. Ops implications:
- We'll need a pre-warmed dedicated pool sized for peak QPS with aggressive KV caching. That means a baseline commit ~3x steady-state capacity for the pilot period.
- Tail latency sources: network variance, GC/host noise, and model decode stalls. Mitigations: colocate model shards near egress, use FP16 + targeted quantization, and enable continuous batching with tight latency SLOs.
- Cross-region active-active is possible but requires sticky routing and health-check granularity at 1s. Failover will still cause transient p95 spikes; to meet contractual 60ms we either limit failover frequency or accept a short carveout window.

Rough cost/capacity estimate attached (ops_burn_estimate.xlsx). Two options we can offer:
A) Strict 60ms p95 (US primary only) — requires dedicated 3x commit, daily cache warms, + 30% premium on top of list pricing.
B) 70ms p95 (US + EU) or 60ms p95 with probabilistic exceptions on failover — lower cost (approx 1.4x baseline).

I can produce a short-runbook and capacity plan but need the traffic histogram and preferred pilot window.

— Vivek
VP, Inference Engineering
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jared Cole <jared.cole@northstarai.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 09:45:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: bespoke availability variance for NorthStarAI

Alex / Marissa,

Legal notes for commercial:
- Please have procurement confirm required start/end dates and any termination triggers tied to availability metrics. Our standard credit calculation favors service credits (monthly) up to a capped % — customer-proposed unilateral credits will need redlines. I've attached a proposed redline of the SLA terms for initial review (proposed_sla_term_redline.docx).
- Any carveouts for failover / force majeure must be explicit and limited to short windows (we should avoid open-ended language).
- Confidentiality: don't include sensitive capacity numbers in external documentation; use ranges where possible.

Marissa — please coordinate with procurement/legal on exposure and pricing levers.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@northstarai.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: bespoke availability variance for NorthStarAI

Jared — thanks for the patience. Internal summary and proposed path:

1) Feasibility: engineering can achieve a p95 ~60ms for US primary with a dedicated pre-warmed pool (Option A) — this carries a non-trivial capacity/cost uplift. Alternative (Option B) is a more economical 70ms or a staged rollout.
2) Legal: redlines attached; we'll negotiate the credit formula and tighten failover carveouts.
3) Proposed pilot: 8-week pilot US-primary dedicated pool, daily cache-warm scripts, joint runbook, and 2-week ramp. If pilot meets 60ms p95 on US primary, we evaluate EU active-active for Phase 2.

Next steps we need from engineering/product (Grace/Vivek/Karthik): short runbook + capacity delta estimate by EOD Tue Mar 12. I'll draft a pilot commercial term sheet and a succinct exec summary to help your procurement. If NorthStar agrees, we can schedule a kick-off next week to lock the pilot window.

Attachments: proposed_sla_term_redline.docx, ops_burn_estimate.xlsx

Best — Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
